text:
Should I Downsize to a Townhome

Hey,
 Been lurking a bit, first post.
 Looking for a sanity check on my plan. I’ve convinced myself that this is the right decision…mostly.
 My wife (55) and I (52) are strongly considering selling our home and buying a townhome. We are empty nesters with fully grown children so downsizing feels natural. My wife has been unemployed since June with benefits running out this December. I am employed with a base salary of $107k/yr ($2k biweekly after all deductions, 401k, ESPP, insurance, etc.). Health insurance is through my job for both of us. We have $40k in an easily accessible emergency fund. We live in Massachusetts.
 Current Home: 4 Bed, 4 Bath, 2,578 sq ft. Valued at $825k. We owe $246k with 18.5 years left on the mortgage at 3.875%. My monthly payment which includes taxes and insurance into escrow is $2,685/mo. I'm worried we'll be unable to keep paying this if my wife remains out of work.
 Townhome we've fallen in love with: 2 Bed, 2 Bath, 2,100 sq ft. Asking price $430k. $420/month HOA. Lakefront. Association pool. Freshwater beach in walking distance. Equal commute to my job. I have the HOA docs and minutes which I've been skimming.
 The plan would be to sell the house and net enough to pay for the townhome without a new mortgage. For simplicity’s sake, not taking closing costs, realtor fees, movers, etc. into account: $825k - $246k = $579k - $430k = $149k remainder.
 I have a current car loan for $23k at 4.9% with 49 payments remaining. I am also repaying student loans for my youngest. Approximately $20k remains with an average interest rate of 4.54%. For simplicity’s sake again, $149k remainder - $23k - $20k = $106k remainder.
 We would then be debt free. My wife could semi-retire and work part-time. This makes financial sense in my head, but I keep second guessing myself.
 Thoughts?
